title: Legislative Branch Agencies Clarification Act
official_title: To modify the appointment and removal process for certain legislative branch officers, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Sponsored by Rep. Griffith (R-VA) with 4 cosponsors; passed the House. The bill reassigns appointment and removal power over the Librarian of Congress, the GPO Director, and the Register of Copyrights, a structural change that faces a 60-vote threshold and likely scrutiny over shifting appointment authority between the branches.
summary: Shifts how Congress's own agency heads are chosen: the Librarian of Congress and the Government Publishing Office Director would be appointed and removed by congressional leaders rather than the President, and the Register of Copyrights would become a Presidential appointee independent of the Library of Congress.
brief: Changes the appointment and removal of the Librarian of Congress, the GPO Director, and the Register of Copyrights.

top_lines.headline: Librarian of Congress Appointed by Congress
subs: Removes the President from appointing the Librarian of Congress
A congressional commission picks from 3 names recommended by oversight committee leaders
Removable at any time by a majority of House and Senate leadership

top_lines.headline: GPO Director Under the Same Model
subs: GPO Director appointed by the congressional commission, not the President
Drops Senate advice-and-consent for the Director
Adds Deputy Director appointment and acting-officer succession rules

top_lines.headline: Copyright Office Split From the Library
subs: Register of Copyrights becomes a Presidential appointee with Senate consent
10-year term, renewable for 5-year terms; must have a copyright-law background
Ratifies Copyright Office actions taken from May 8, 2025 through enactment

items.main: Names the Act the “Legislative Branch Agencies Clarification Act”.
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

items.main: Replaces Presidential appointment of the Librarian of Congress with appointment by a congressional commission.
items.detail: Amends the Librarian of Congress Succession Modernization Act of 2015. A vacancy is filled by 'oversight committee leadership' (the chair and ranking member of the House Committee on House Administration and the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration) jointly recommending 3 individuals, from whom the 'House and Senate leadership' (the Speaker, the Senate majority leader, and the House and Senate minority leaders) selects the Librarian by majority vote, without regard to political affiliation. The Librarian may be removed at any time by a majority vote of the House and Senate leadership, and is no longer treated as a political appointee for purposes of section 747 of the Financial Services and General Government Appropriations Act, 2024.

items.main: Creates a Deputy Librarian of Congress and an acting-Librarian succession line.
items.detail: The Librarian must appoint a Deputy Librarian within 120 days of being appointed or of a vacancy arising. If the Librarian fails to do so, the oversight committee leadership recommends an individual whom the House and Senate leadership appoint by majority vote. The Deputy Librarian acts as Librarian during an absence, disability, or vacancy; if both positions are empty, the leadership designates an acting Librarian.

sections.label: Section 4 — Director of the Government Publishing Office

items.main: Applies the same commission-appointment and leadership-removal model to the GPO Director.
items.detail: Amends chapter 3 of title 44, U.S. Code. The Director of the Government Publishing Office is appointed by the congressional commission from 3 individuals recommended by the oversight committee leadership, striking the prior 'by and with the advice and consent of the Senate' language, and may be removed at any time by a majority vote of the House and Senate leadership. The Director is likewise no longer treated as a political appointee for the same appropriations-law purpose.

sections.label: Section 5 — Deputy Director of the Government Publishing Office

items.main: Establishes a Deputy Director of the GPO with acting-Director succession rules.
items.detail: Rewrites sections 302 and 304 of title 44 so the Director appoints a Deputy Director (within 120 days of appointment or a vacancy), with a leadership-appointment fallback if the Director does not act, and the Deputy Director serves as acting Director during an absence, disability, or vacancy.

items.main: Removes the Library of Congress supervisory authority over the Copyright Office and makes the Register of Copyrights a Presidential appointee.
items.detail: Amends title 17, U.S. Code, replacing the Librarian of Congress with the Register of Copyrights across many provisions. The Register would be appointed by the President with the advice and consent of the Senate after the chair and ranking member of four committees (the House Committee on House Administration, the House Committee on the Judiciary, the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration, and the Senate Committee on the Judiciary) jointly recommend 3 individuals; the Register must be a U.S. citizen with a background in copyright law, serves a 10-year term, and may be reappointed for additional 5-year terms. It establishes a standalone Office of Inspector General within the Copyright Office, whose Inspector General is appointed by, reports to, and is removable by the Register of Copyrights (on 30 days' written notice to the House and Senate oversight and appropriations committees) and holds audit, investigation, and law-enforcement authority, and ratifies actions taken by the Copyright Office, the Register, the Copyright Royalty Judges, and the Copyright Claims Board between May 8, 2025 and the date of enactment. A transition period running through September 30, 2029 lets the Register and the Librarian transfer appropriated funds to one another to effectuate the Copyright Office's separation from the Library, and the Library of Congress and other legislative-branch offices may provide administrative and other support to the Copyright Office under service agreements.

sections.label: Section 7 — Government Publishing Office Personnel Reforms

items.main: Brings the GPO under the Congressional Accountability Act of 1995.
items.detail: Adds the Government Publishing Office to the entities covered by section 101(a) of the Congressional Accountability Act of 1995 and makes conforming amendments to title 5 that remove the GPO from several executive-branch personnel provisions.

sections.label: Section 8 — Human Capital Management System for the GPO

items.main: Directs the GPO Director to establish a merit-based human capital management system.
items.detail: Adds a new section 306A to title 44 requiring the Director to establish and maintain a human capital system that incorporates the merit-system principles of section 2301(b) of title 5, prohibits the prohibited personnel practices and political activity barred under title 5, appoints and promotes employees only on merit and fitness, and gives a hiring preference to individuals eligible for a hiring preference in the executive branch, to an extent consistent with the preference they would receive there. Regulations require public notice and comment and the approval of the Joint Committee on Printing.

items.main: Updates which entities the GPO may provide printing and publishing services to.
items.detail: Rewrites section 501 of title 44 so the Government Publishing Office may perform printing, binding, blank-book work, and publishing services for Congress, the Executive Office of the President, the Judiciary, and every executive department, independent office, and establishment of the Government, and repeals a 1993 conforming provision.

items.main: Sets when the appointment and removal changes apply.
items.detail: The new appointment procedures apply to appointments made on or after enactment, while the new removal provisions apply to individuals serving before, on, or after enactment — meaning current officeholders become removable under the new leadership-vote standard.
If any provision of the Act or any amendment it makes is held unconstitutional, the remainder of the Act, and its application to any other person or circumstance, is not affected.

underreported: Actions taken by the Copyright Office, the Register, the Copyright Royalty Judges, and the Copyright Claims Board between May 8, 2025 and enactment would be ratified and given full force and effect.

The Copyright Office's new Office of Inspector General would carry law-enforcement authority: its supervisory special agents and the special agents they supervise could make warrantless arrests, execute arrest, search, and seizure warrants, and carry firearms while on duty.
gaps: The bill does not specify what happens if the oversight committee leaders cannot agree on the 3 individuals to recommend for a vacancy.
Removal of the Librarian and the GPO Director 'at any time' by a leadership majority sets no for-cause standard or fixed term of office.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Morelle
featured_quotes.text: Again, let me thank the sponsor of the bill, my friend Mr. Griffith, for his hard work.

added: A congressional commission and House/Senate leadership vote to appoint and remove the Librarian of Congress and the GPO Director; an Inspector General for the Copyright Office; a merit-based human capital system for the GPO
modified: Register of Copyrights becomes a Presidential appointee (with Senate consent) independent of the Librarian of Congress, with a 10-year renewable term; Librarian and GPO Director appointments drop Presidential nomination and Senate advice-and-consent
removed: Library of Congress supervisory authority over the Copyright Office; Senate advice-and-consent for the Librarian of Congress and the GPO Director

added: New Sec. 11 Severability clause added — unconstitutional provisions severed without affecting the rest of the Act

Sec. 6(g) Transition Provisions added — through September 30, 2029, Register and Librarian may transfer appropriations to effectuate the Copyright Office/Library separation, plus personnel-law transition rules

Copyright Office Inspector General now established as a separate Office of Inspector General with detailed appointment, removal (30-day written notice), pay (above GS-15, no bonuses), law-enforcement (arrest/firearm) authority, peer review, and budget-independence provisions

Section 702 amendment now inserts language requiring the Register to consult the Librarian before regulations affecting deposits under sections 407 and 704 or the Library's access to deposited material
modified: Register of Copyrights nominee recommendation now requires joint recommendation from chair/ranking member of four committees (House Administration, House Judiciary, Senate Rules and Administration, Senate Judiciary) instead of just the two Judiciary Committees
Sec. 7 GPO personnel reforms restructured — Congressional Accountability Act application and conforming title 5 amendments reorganized into separate lettered subsections
removed: Original Sec. 6(c) two-paragraph Inspector General approach (amending title 5 sec. 415 and adding a 'no oversight authority' clause to sec. 1307) replaced by the new standalone IG office
